meta.area_weighting: Per-OSID areas from data/derived/operational/osid_areas.json (as src/sim/osid_areas.ts); municipality area = sum of its OSIDs; total 51,337 km2

confidence_enum.documented: read from a primary map/text cited in source (UN S-documents, UN DPI maps) or stated by ICTY/UN/BB
confidence_enum.inferred: derived by a stated rule, or a map reading whose minority share may be measurement noise

method_notes.vance_owen: Province membership read from the signed 25 Mar 1993 revised map in S/25479 (municipality names printed, province borders thick). Provinces 1,5,9 -> RBiH; 2,4,6 -> RS; 3,8,10 -> HRHB; 7 -> special. These leads are confirmed by the S/25479 rule (governor = most numerous people, 1991 census): computed governors are Bosniak in 1,5,7,9; Serb in 2,4,6; Croat in 3,8,10. Split fractions = flood-fill pixel areas on the scan.
method_notes.owen_stoltenberg: 20 Aug 1993 Geneva map (S/26337 App. I) georeferenced and intersected with OSID polygons; shares per municipality in map_share_pct. Sketch-map accuracy +-5 km, so minority shares below ~15% may be artefacts. Invincible (20 Sep) changes are textual only (S/26486) and not drawn.
method_notes.contact_group: UN map 4128 georeferenced (2nd order, residual <= ~6 px = ~1 km) and classified by grey shade per OSID; threshold chosen where the totals reproduce the published 51/49 (Federation 48.2 + neutral 2.9 vs RS 48.9). Faction layer inside the Federation inferred.
method_notes.dayton: Unchanged from v1: entity per municipality from the post-1995 municipal structure (documented).

sources.KORDIC-TJ: ICTY Kordic & Cerkez Trial Judgement (IT-95-14/2-T, 26 Feb 2001), Part III ch.IV: Province 10 = Travnik, Novi Travnik, Vitez, Busovaca, Fojnica, Gornji Vakuf, part of Kiseljak
sources.BLASKIC-TJ: ICTY Blaskic Trial Judgement (IT-95-14-T, 3 Mar 2000): Lasva valley mostly Province 10; southern Kiseljak to Province 7; Province 8 from the Croatian border north to Prozor and Konjic; Croats main responsibility in 8 and 10, Muslims in 7

sources.A/54/549: UN SG report "The fall of Srebrenica" A/54/549 (15 Nov 1999): Province 5 Bosniac-majority, included Srebrenica and Zepa and most of the areas of eastern Bosnia recently ethnically cleansed
sources.IZIZ: Univ. of Sarajevo Institute for Research of Crimes against Humanity, "Srebrenica 1992-1995" (secondary): VOPP province including Foca, Visegrad, Srebrenica, Gorazde and Zvornik unacceptable to Serb representatives
sources.MEARSHEIMER-PAPE: Mearsheimer & Pape, "The Answer", New Republic 14 Jun 1993: Gorazde and Tuzla among Muslim areas from which Serbs would have to withdraw under VOPP
sources.POSAVINA-ORG: posavina.org (secondary, local): VOPP Province 3 = Derventa, Bosanski Brod, Odzak, Modrica, Bosanski Samac, Brcko, Orasje plus parts of Gradacac and Doboj
sources.OS-TEXT: Agreement relating to BiH / Constitutional Agreement of the Union of Republics of BiH (Owen-Stoltenberg, "Invincible" package, text dated 16 Sep 1993; S/26337/Add.1 and S/26486 annex) via peaceagreements.org: Muslim-majority republic not less than 30% of Union territory; Gorazde-Zepa road part of Muslim republic; access to Sava (rail line across Brcko to the Sava bridge) and to the sea at Neum / Ploce
sources.BB1-50: Balkan Battlegrounds I chronology KB BB1_p0050: Abdic APWB recognized by Serbs "on the basis of the Geneva plan"
sources.CG-SEC: Contact Group map (Geneva, 6 Jul 1994): UN Digital Library map record 705480 ("Bosnian Serb Republic, Muslim-Croat Federation and neutral zone"); Australian Parliament JFADT Bosnia report ch.4; secondary summaries: Serbs to cede ~22% of the territory they held, Srebrenica, Zepa and Gorazde assigned to the Federation, Gorazde linked by corridor, Brcko demilitarised
sources.GFAP-A2: GFAP Annex 2 (IEBL) as implemented; repo data/source/municipality_post1995_to_mun1990.json (BHAS post-1995 municipal codes: 1xxxx=FBiH, 2xxxx=RS, 3xxxx=Brcko District); split shares from data/derived/municipality_borders.geojson areas
sources.GFAP-A2-V: GFAP Annex 2 Article V (Brcko arbitration within one year); Final Award 5 Mar 1999 -> Brcko District (8 Mar 2000)
sources.BB1-1995: Balkan Battlegrounds I, KB pages BB1_p0402-p0427 (1995 western offensives: Grahovo/Glamoc 28 Jul; Donji Vakuf 10-14 Sep; Drvar, Petrovac, Kljuc Sep; Sanski Most / Mrkonjic Grad Oct 1995)
sources.OHR-1996: OHR Chronology 1996: inter-entity transfers at D+45 (3 Feb 1996) around Sarajevo and "the anvil" around Mrkonjic Grad; Sarajevo suburbs (Vogosca 24 Feb ... Grbavica 18-19 Mar 1996) to Federation
sources.RULE-VOPP-MAJ: INFERENCE: VOPP provinces were "largely determined by ethnicity" (BB1-42 chronology); assigned by 1991 majority + contiguity with the documented province capital
sources.RULE-OS-FRONT: INFERENCE: the Aug-Sep 1993 Owen-Stoltenberg map was a "thinly veiled partition" (BB1-219) that largely followed the summer-1993 front line; assigned to the party holding the municipality in Aug 1993
sources.RULE-CG-HELD: INFERENCE: the Contact Group map only took territory from the Serbs (Federation 51% vs ~30% held); Federation-held municipalities assumed Federation; RS-held core areas far from the documented cessions assumed RS
sources.RULE-FED-LAYER: INFERENCE (faction layer only): Federation land assigned to RBiH or HRHB by the party administering it at war end / Washington-Agreement canton (Croat-majority cantons 2, 8, 10; HDZ-run municipalities in mixed cantons 6, 7). Dayton itself does not divide the Federation between Bosniaks and Croats.
sources.S/25479-MAP: UN S/25479 (26 Mar 1993) Annex I Appendix A / Annex III: revised provisional provincial map signed 25 Mar 1993 by Izetbegovic and Boban, witnessed Vance and Owen (municipality-labelled map with province borders; read visually from the scanned page, digitallibrary.un.org/record/164852)
sources.S/25479-TEXT: UN S/25479 para 10 (Sarajevo province enlarged: most of Kiseljak and Kresevo as in original map + whole opstinas Visoko, Breza, Vares + small border area of Kakanj); Annex I sec. C (capital city = built-up parts of Novi Grad, Centar, Novo Sarajevo, Stari Grad), sec. D (governor = most numerous constituent people of the province, 1991 census), sec. E (withdrawal of forces), App. D (Access Authority throughways: Han Pijesak-Sekovici and Sekovici-Zvornik pass through Tuzla Province; Pale-Kalinovik passes through Sarajevo Province; Foca-Sarajevo passes through East Herzegovina Province; Zvornik is the Tuzla Province border crossing)
sources.UN-4129: UN DPI Map No. 4129 (Nov 1999) "Vance-Owen Peace Plan as presented January 1993" (digitallibrary.un.org/record/705482)
sources.S/26337-MAP: UN S/26337 (20 Aug 1993) Appendix I map "Union of Republics of Bosnia and Herzegovina" (digitallibrary.un.org/record/173639), georeferenced on 9 town dots (affine, residual ~3-9 km) and intersected with repo OSID polygons
sources.S/26337-TEXT: UN S/26337 paras 5-6: Sarajevo under UN administration up to two years, Mostar under EC administration; detailed Brcko demarcation (appendix III); Serb side agreed a Gorazde-Zepa road as Muslim-republic territory
sources.S/26260: UN S/26260 (6 Aug 1993): Constitutional Agreement of the Union of Republics (text), annex A part II (Neum + southern Stolac, Brcko railway to the Sava, Union buildings in Sarajevo vested in the Union), paras 30-41 (30% floor; Serbs call it an ~18% roll-back; Brcko access line; Gorazde link; Zepa-Srebrenica enlarged 100%; Bihac pocket; Lasva boundary proposal; Sarajevo positions)
sources.S/26486: UN S/26486 (23 Sep 1993): HMS Invincible agreements of 20 Sep 1993 (Neum throughway Poplat-Neum, land on Kosa/Klek, Neretva port Visici-Celjevo, Muslim southern border moved from Recice to above Visici, Ploce 99-year lease, extra Muslim land on the Drina between Gorazde and Visegrad, future Prevlaka/Dubrovnik exchange)
sources.S/1994/173: UN S/1994/173 (14 Feb 1994): Serb map offering the Muslim-majority republic 33.56%; Presidency target 33.3%; Croats asked recognition of 17.5%; Mostar to EU, Sarajevo to UN; disputed areas to arbitration
sources.UN-4128: UN DPI Map No. 4128 (Nov 1999) "Contact Group July 1994 Proposal" (Bosnian Serb Republic / Muslim-Croat Federation / Neutral zone), digitallibrary.un.org/record/705480; georeferenced on 12 town circles (2nd-order fit, residual <=1-2 km) and classified per OSID by map shade (threshold calibrated so that totals reproduce 51/49)

brcko.note: Brcko (town and east, ~70% of drawn area) in Province 4 with Bijeljina. A separately-outlined narrow strip (~30%) runs from the Sava between Orasje and Brcko south toward Srebrenik; it is not numbered on the map. Most likely the Tuzla-Orasje access corridor (App. D lists the Tuzla-Orasje and Tuzla-Brcko roads through Posavina and Bijeljina provinces as Access Authority throughways). Status unlabelled. Split percentages = flood-filled pixel areas on the scanned map (approximate).
